references.text: Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran, which establishes the timeline of his life – eleven years before Ishmael's birth when Abram was 86.
The preceding verse states that Hagar bore a son to Abram, and that Abram named him Ishmael – the direct context for the age given in verse 16.
When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord appeared to him – thirteen years after Ishmael's birth, providing a timeline of events in Abram's life.
Abram was ninety-nine when he was circumcised, and Ishmael was thirteen – this confirms the age relationship established in 16:16.
Abraham was one hundred years old when his son Isaac was born, meaning that fourteen years passed between Ishmael's birth (when Abram was 86) and Isaac's birth.
Ishmael's descendants and his death are listed, showing the completion of Abraham's family history that began with Ishmael's birth in chapter 16.
Paul uses the story of Sarah and Hagar, Isaac and Ishmael, as an allegory for the difference between law and promise, offering a New Testament perspective on the events surrounding Ishmael's birth.
Theological contrast between Ishmael's birth (human plan) and Isaac's birth (God's promise).
